Definition: according to most a plumb-line, and to others a hook
BiblicalUsage: The word appears twice, both times in Amos's vision: the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in His hand, and said, 'Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more.' A plumbline is a builder's line with a weight on it, held against a wall to see whether it stands straight — and God holds it against Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: Two verses about a plumbline carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the measuring — God holding His line against His people and finding the wall crooked.
